classification.difficultyReason: Recognise that the given amount is interest alone, subtract one from the five-year growth multiplier, and reverse that multiplier to find the principal.

content.prompt: An investment at an interest rate of $10\%$ p.a., compounded annually, returned interest of $\$40\,000$ after five years. Calculate the original amount invested, correct to the nearest cent.

answer.short:
$\$65\,518.99$.

Divide the interest by $(1.10)^5-1$, since the interest excludes the original principal.
answer.worked:
Let the original investment be $P$ dollars. The final amount is $P(1.10)^5$, so:
$$\begin{aligned}\text{Interest}&=P(1.10)^5-P\\40\,000&=P\big((1.10)^5-1\big)\\40\,000&=0.61051P\\P&=40\,000\div0.61051\\P&\approx65\,518.99\end{aligned}$$
The original investment was $\$65\,518.99$, correct to the nearest cent.
